milestones.description: First useful version (Windows): documented protocol, static color, brightness, recovery after sleep/resume and replugging, minimal tray.
Screen mirroring on Windows: per-LED frames, DXGI capture, monitor choice, zone layout, smoothing.
Linux: X11 and Wayland capture, suspend/resume and hotplug recovery, NixOS flake.
Full settings window and quality: preview, calibration, color processing, HDR, notifications.
Stabilization: installers, nixpkgs, user documentation, full release checklist.

items.title: Initialize the strip as documented in the protocol spec
items.summary: Send the init/handshake sequence the strip needs before it accepts color data, as derived from captures.
done_when: The sequence is documented in docs/protocol.md with the captures it comes from
Encoders in device/protocol.py are tested against fixtures from real captures
The device manager sends it after every open and reopen

items.title: Set the whole strip to one color
items.summary: Encode and send a single color for all LEDs.
done_when: The color report is documented in docs/protocol.md
Encoder is fixture-tested; behaviour is checked on the real strip

items.title: Brightness control
items.summary: Set brightness through the device's own control if the protocol has one, otherwise by scaling colors in software.
done_when: Captures show whether the strip has a brightness command (05-brightness-change)
Brightness 0-100% works in static mode and is kept across reconnects

items.title: Turn the strip on and off
items.summary: Switch the strip off and back on, restoring the previous state.
done_when: The power report (or the documented equivalent) is in docs/protocol.md
Off/on from CLI and tray restores the last color and brightness

items.title: Rate-limit writes to the strip
items.summary: Never write faster than a configurable cap (default 60 fps), dropping or merging excess frames.
done_when: Limiter is unit-tested with a fake clock against FakeTransport
The cap is a setting with a safe default

items.title: LED count setting
items.summary: The number of LEDs is a user setting (strips can be cut); it is never hard-coded.
done_when: Setting with default 75 and validation, used by every encoder
Changing it applies without restarting the app

items.title: Reconnect after unplugging and replugging (Windows)
items.summary: Notice device arrival/removal and reopen the strip automatically.
done_when: Write errors and device removal close the handle cleanly
Device arrival triggers reopen, re-init and restore of the last state
Verified on hardware by replugging while the app runs

items.title: Recover the strip after sleep/resume (Windows)
items.summary: The reason this project exists: after waking from sleep the strip must come back without user action.
done_when: Windows power events (RegisterSuspendResumeNotification / WM_POWERBROADCAST) reach the device manager
On resume: close, wait for re-enumeration, reopen with backoff, re-init, restore state; never on the UI thread
Captures and notes (08-sleep-resume) explain what the device does around sleep, including the Code 28 state
Verified on hardware over repeated sleep/resume cycles

items.title: Device driver abstraction and registry
items.summary: Each supported device is a driver behind a common interface; a registry maps VID/PID to drivers, so other devices can be added later.
done_when: Engine and UI talk to a generic device (LED count, capabilities), not to one strip's protocol
The strip's protocol is the first driver; tests use a fake driver

items.title: Static color mode
items.summary: The engine's first mode: hold one color and brightness, re-applied after every reconnect.
done_when: Mode is selectable from CLI and tray and persisted in settings

items.title: Minimal tray icon
items.summary: Tray icon with on/off, color, brightness, device status and quit. The full settings window comes in 0.4.
done_when: Tray works on Windows; UI talks to the engine only through the facade, core never imports Qt
Shows when the strip is disconnected or recovering

items.title: Start with Windows
items.summary: Optional autostart at login so recovery works after every boot.
done_when: Setting toggles autostart for the current user; works for the zip build

items.title: Persist settings in TOML
items.summary: Settings model saved to a TOML file in the platform config directory (platformdirs).
done_when: Typed settings model with defaults and validation; unknown keys are kept or reported, not crashing
Round-trip tests

items.title: Allow only one running instance
items.summary: A second launch must not fight the first one for the device; it brings the running instance forward or exits.
done_when: Second instance detects the first and exits cleanly (tested)

items.title: CLI: set color, on/off, run headless
items.summary: rimlight-cli commands for scripting and debugging: set-color, brightness, on, off, and run (engine without UI).
done_when: Commands documented in --help and README; tested against FakeTransport

items.title: Log to a file and copy diagnostics
items.summary: Rotating log file and a way to collect diagnostics for bug reports, with serials masked.
done_when: Logs include device events, power events and recovery steps with timestamps
Tray/CLI action copies diagnostics (version, OS, masked device list, recent log)

items.title: Turn the strip off on sleep, shutdown and exit (Windows)
items.summary: The strip goes dark when the PC sleeps or shuts down and when rimlight exits (configurable).
done_when: Behaviour is configurable and verified on hardware

items.title: Detect the LED count automatically
items.summary: If the protocol exposes the LED count, use it as the default; the manual setting (A12) stays as an override.
done_when: Captures show whether the device reports its length; if not, close this as not possible and rely on calibration (C2)

items.title: Dump sent reports from the CLI
items.summary: A debug option that prints every report rimlight sends, to compare with captures.
done_when: rimlight-cli option logs reports as hex with timestamps; never sends anything by itself

items.title: Per-LED color frames
items.summary: Send a different color to every LED in one frame.
done_when: Frame layout (LED order, channel order, multi-report frames) documented in docs/protocol.md
Encoder fixture-tested; verified on hardware with test patterns

items.title: Screen capture on Windows (DXGI)
items.summary: CaptureBackend using DXGI Desktop Duplication.
done_when: Frames delivered at the configured rate; handles display mode changes and sleep/resume

items.title: Choose the monitor to mirror
items.summary: With several monitors, the user picks which one the strip follows.
done_when: Monitor list with names; choice persisted; survives monitor reordering where possible

items.title: Keep CPU and GPU load low while mirroring
items.summary: rimlight runs all the time, so mirroring must be cheap: downscaled capture, configurable rate.
done_when: Load is measured and documented on a reference machine; capture rate is a setting

items.title: Zone layout: start corner, direction, LEDs per edge
items.summary: Map LED indices to screen regions from the strip's physical layout.
done_when: Layout settings cover start corner, direction and LED count per edge; mapping is unit-tested

items.title: Smoothing between frames
items.summary: Smooth color changes to avoid flicker; speed is configurable.
done_when: Smoothing is unit-tested and configurable

items.title: Configurable zone depth
items.summary: How far into the screen each zone samples.
done_when: Depth setting applied by the mapping, with tests

items.title: Screen capture on Linux X11
items.summary: CaptureBackend using XShm (mss).
done_when: Works on an X11 session; selected automatically by the backend factory

items.title: Screen capture on Linux Wayland
items.summary: CaptureBackend using xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast and PipeWire.
done_when: Works on GNOME and KDE at least; portal permission is remembered where the portal allows it

items.title: Reconnect after unplugging and replugging (Linux)
items.summary: udev/hidraw hotplug triggers reopen, re-init and restore.
done_when: Verified on hardware with the udev rule installed

items.title: Recover the strip after suspend/resume (Linux)
items.summary: logind PrepareForSleep drives the same recovery path as on Windows.
done_when: Verified on hardware over repeated suspend/resume cycles

items.title: Start with the desktop session (Linux)
items.summary: Optional autostart via XDG autostart (and the NixOS module).
done_when: Setting toggles autostart; works on GNOME and KDE

items.title: NixOS flake with package and module
items.summary: flake.nix in the repository with a package and a NixOS module (udev rule, optional autostart). The PyInstaller tarball does not run on NixOS.
done_when: nix build works and is checked in CI; module documented in README

items.title: Turn the strip off on suspend, shutdown and exit (Linux)
items.summary: Linux counterpart of A10, using logind inhibitor locks.
done_when: Behaviour is configurable and verified on hardware

items.title: Main settings window
items.summary: Full window for every setting, so nobody needs to edit TOML.
done_when: Every setting is reachable in the window; pytest-qt tests for the main flows

items.title: Live LED preview
items.summary: Show what the strip displays, around a monitor outline.
done_when: Preview follows the engine output without slowing it down

items.title: Calibration wizard
items.summary: Light LEDs one by one so the user finds the start corner, direction and edge counts without counting.
done_when: Wizard produces a complete zone layout (C1)

items.title: Gamma, white balance and color temperature
items.summary: Color correction so the strip matches the screen.
done_when: Settings with sane defaults; processing is unit-tested

items.title: Threshold for dark scenes
items.summary: Keep near-black scenes from producing flickering murky colors.
done_when: Threshold setting, unit-tested

items.title: Correct colors on HDR monitors
items.summary: Tone-map HDR captures so colors are not washed out.
done_when: Verified on an HDR display

items.title: Notifications on disconnect and recovery
items.summary: Optional desktop notifications when the strip is lost or recovered.
done_when: Notifications can be turned off; no notification storms during repeated reconnects

items.title: Windows installer
items.summary: Installer (MSI and/or winget) with Start menu entry and uninstall.
done_when: Built by the release workflow and attached to releases

items.title: Package rimlight in nixpkgs
items.summary: Submit the package (and module) to nixpkgs once a stable version exists.
done_when: Package merged into nixpkgs

items.title: React to screen lock
items.summary: Optionally dim or turn off the strip while the session is locked.
done_when: Configurable behaviour on Windows and Linux

items.title: Drive several strips at once
items.summary: Support more than one strip, for example on several monitors.
done_when: Each strip has its own layout and monitor

items.title: Show the firmware version
items.summary: Display the strip's firmware version, if the protocol reports it.
done_when: Shown in CLI and diagnostics

items.title: Support other Nanoleaf devices
items.summary: Add drivers for other devices once owners or captures are available (clean-room: each device needs its own captures).
done_when: One issue per device, each with its own protocol documentation

items.title: Ignore letterbox bars
items.summary: Detect black bars in films and sample the picture instead.
done_when: Detection is stable and unit-tested on sample frames

items.title: Saturation boost
items.summary: Optional saturation increase for more vivid ambient light.
done_when: Setting, unit-tested

items.title: Built-in effects
items.summary: Original effects such as rainbow or breathing. Never copies the vendor's effect definitions.
done_when: Effects selectable from tray and window

items.title: Schedules: night mode and timed off
items.summary: Change brightness or turn the strip off at set times.
done_when: Schedule settings, tested with a fake clock

items.title: Profiles and presets
items.summary: Save and switch named sets of settings.
done_when: Profiles selectable from tray and window

items.title: Global hotkeys
items.summary: Keyboard shortcuts for on/off, mode and brightness.
done_when: Configurable hotkeys on Windows and Linux X11 (Wayland where possible)

items.title: Translate the user interface
items.summary: Qt translations, starting with Russian.
done_when: Translation workflow documented; UI strings extracted

items.title: Local API for automation
items.summary: Local HTTP/WebSocket (and D-Bus on Linux) API for Home Assistant and scripts.
done_when: Bound to localhost by default; documented

items.title: Per-application profiles
items.summary: Switch profile or mode when a given application or game runs.
done_when: Rules configurable; works on Windows

items.title: Flatpak, AUR and deb packages
items.summary: Native packages for common Linux distributions.
done_when: One issue per package format when someone picks it up

items.title: Check for updates
items.summary: Optional check against GitHub Releases; never downloads or installs by itself.
done_when: Off by default or clearly opt-in; respects pre-release channel choice
